statement: Researchers must personally check every citation an AI tool gives them before they submit a paper.
Using AI to polish writing you drafted yourself is different from having AI write the draft.
Journals should require authors to say how they used AI in writing a paper.
AI makes it easier for non-native English speakers to compete in science publishing.
Students learn to write better when they practice with AI than without it.
Journals should use AI as the first reviewer on every submitted paper.
Caps on how many papers one person can submit are a fair response to the flood of AI-written papers.
AI-polished writing is erasing scientists' personal and cultural voices, and that is a real loss.
A paper mostly written by AI is still the scientist's own work if the ideas are theirs.
Plain-language AI summaries of research do more good than harm, even when they lose nuance.
